cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: smallest k with cumulative binomial >= 0.75 for 6 trials at p=0.5
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 4. Independently derived by tabulating the cumulative binomial for n=6, p=0.5: k=0 -> 0.015625, k=1 -> 0.109375, k=2 -> 0.34375, k=3 -> 0.65625, k=4 -> 0.890625. The first k whose cumulative probability reaches the 0.75 criterion is 4

cases.description: A criterion value exactly equal to a cumulative probability, testing the documented >= comparison
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "the smallest value for which the cumulative binomial distribution is greater than or equal to a criterion value". The cumulative probability at k=3 is exactly 42/64 = 0.65625, so a >= comparison returns 3 while a strict > comparison would return 4 -- this case separates the two

cases.description: A non-integer trials argument, which the documentation says is truncated
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "If trials is not an integer, it is truncated", so 6.9 must behave as 6 and return the documented 4. Independently checked that this discriminates: with n=7 the cumulative reaches 0.75 first at k=4 as well, but the underlying distribution differs, so this case is paired with the doc example rather than standing alone
Excel documents: "If alpha <= 0 or alpha => 1, BINOM.INV returns the #NUM! error value."
Excel documents: "If probability_s is <= 0 or probability_s => 1, BINOM.INV returns the #NUM! error value." Note that unlike BINOM.DIST, the endpoints 0 and 1 are EXCLUDED here
